title: Minor - C# "Missing Connected Method" warning doesn't disappear after fixing the issue.
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible in 4.5.1 RC 1 ### System information Godot v4.5.1.rc1.mono - Windows 11 (build 26100) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.8088) - AMD Ryzen 9 5950X 16-Core Processor (32 threads) - 127.9 GiB memory ### Issue description If you create an Area2D signal (via "signals" in the editor) and with C# code, the c# code editor (in Godot) tells you on compile that there is a missing connected method (as it should) However, if you ADD the correct method, the warning doesnt go away (even though the signal now happens). This can get confusing when you're trying to debug code, and trying to figure out which signals are connected or not. ### Steps to reproduce Create Simple C# project. Create An object, add a C# Script. Create an Area2D as a child, and set up collision shape/etc as normal On the Area2D, go to "Node", then "Signals" Under "body_entered" Create a new signal You'll be told: **C# : Callback code won't be generated, please add it manually** Now press "connect" Go to the C# Script in the godot editor, and hit build. You'll see the warning: **_Missing connected method 'FunctionName' for signal 'body_entered' from node 'Node2D/CharacterBody2D/HitBox' to node ''Node2D/CharacterBody2D'_** (or similar, depending on how you set up your tree) Now, add the missing FunctionName, etc. And build again. the code will now work, and you'll have zero warnings, in the build window. But the warning window will still show "Missing connected method" I've added a visual here: Red #1 : Function Name added Red #2 : Callback happening (can now play sound effect) Red #3 : Warning disappeared from build Red #4 : Still seeing the warning message, with the warning number (i.e. the yellow triangle with !) in the warning window. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) will do later, it's a minor issue for me.. But something which is confusing at first.
